subsystems.name: Individual robot unit
subsystems.role: a cheap, simple agent that can move, sense and decide on its own.

subsystems.name: Onboard sensing
subsystems.role: lets each robot know where it is and what is nearby, without central control.

subsystems.name: Local communication mesh
subsystems.role: robots exchange positions, task claims and warnings directly with neighbours.

subsystems.name: Decentralised control layer
subsystems.role: local rules produce useful group behaviour — no robot has the whole picture.

subsystems.name: Operator interface
subsystems.role: a human sets the goal and monitors, but does not steer each robot.

subsystems.name: Energy and docking infrastructure
subsystems.role: keeps hundreds of small robots running without manual battery swaps.

buildSteps.title: Define the task and its grain
buildSteps.detail: Decide what the swarm must achieve and what each individual robot can sense and do, because the group can only be as capable as its simplest member.

buildSteps.title: Design the single robot
buildSteps.detail: Build one cheap, robust unit — small motors, basic sensors, a radio and a battery — since swarms buy redundancy by number, not by quality.

buildSteps.title: Write the local rules
buildSteps.detail: Specify the handful of neighbour-relative behaviours (move apart, align, move toward a goal, claim a task) that should add up to the desired group result.

buildSteps.title: Simulate at scale
buildSteps.detail: Run thousands of virtual agents in a physics simulator to find the parameter settings that avoid deadlock, oscillation and pile-ups before any hardware is built.

buildSteps.title: Test a small fleet indoors
buildSteps.detail: Five to twenty real robots on a flat floor with motion-capture or ultra-wideband tracking to check that simulation and reality agree.

buildSteps.title: Add the mesh network
buildSteps.detail: Tune radio range, message rate and time synchronisation so the fleet keeps communicating as it spreads out and robots leave and rejoin.

buildSteps.title: Trial outdoors
buildSteps.detail: Move to a field or disaster-training site with GNSS-denied zones, wind, uneven ground and a safety operator holding a kill switch.

buildSteps.title: Scale and automate logistics
buildSteps.detail: Add docking stations, fleet-health monitoring and spare-robot swapping so the swarm can run for days rather than minutes.

prerequisites.why: the economics only work if losing individual robots is cheap.
robots must coordinate without a single base station that can fail or run out of range.
indoors, underground and under canopy, robots need ultra-wideband or vision to know where they are.
auction and consensus methods work in the lab but scale poorly when hundreds of robots and tight deadlines meet.

prerequisites.tech: Battery energy density and safe fast charging
prerequisites.why: small robots carry little energy, so mission length is set by power, not by intelligence.

prerequisites.tech: Rules for flying many autonomous aircraft at once
prerequisites.why: beyond visual line of sight and over people, approvals are still granted case by case.

pathway.milestone: warehouse fleets of hundreds of robots moving goods, and synchronised drone light shows
pathway.unlocks: proven coordination and traffic control at scale on constrained tasks.

pathway.milestone: cooperative inspection and agricultural swarms working fields and structures
pathway.unlocks: commercial value in mapping, spraying and monitoring large areas.

pathway.milestone: heterogeneous search-and-rescue teams — ground, aerial and water robots sharing a map
pathway.unlocks: faster coverage of disaster sites too dangerous or too large for people.

pathway.milestone: self-sustaining swarms for environmental monitoring, wildfire response and construction
pathway.unlocks: persistent coverage of the physical world without a human per robot.
